record.title: HiVe-Mem reports adaptive multimodal-memory retrieval with lower token use
record.summary: Zhang et al. introduce HiVe-Mem, which expands semantically retrieved interaction episodes through a text-and-visual affinity graph, then uses a PPO-trained selector to choose evidence forms per retrieved episode. In a preprint, they report higher F1 and LLM-judge scores than the compared multimodal memory systems on Mem-Gallery, WorldMemArena's Lifelong subset, and H2HMem, with 89.8–91.6% lower average token use than the most token-efficient multimodal baselines. These are author-reported benchmark results; the paper excludes adversarial settings, uses GPT-4o-mini for LLM judging, and has not been independently reproduced. The linked repository exposes implementation and experiment instructions, but the research desk did not run it.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record shows HiVe-Mem was submitted on 2026-11-09 and provides a v1 paper with methods, benchmark tables, appendix details and a linked code repository.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that HiVe-Mem improves average task scores across three multimodal memory benchmarks and uses 89.8–91.6% fewer tokens than the most token-efficient multimodal baselines in their two-model evaluation.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent reproduction, performance on adversarial settings, transfer beyond the evaluated benchmarks and two base models, or improved outcomes in deployed long-horizon agent workloads.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported benchmark scores and token reductions have not been independently reproduced from the linked repository.
Adversarial cases, broader model families, full WorldMemArena coverage and real long-running agent workloads are outside the reported evaluation.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced, query-adaptive retrieval and evidence selection that improve multimodal-memory benchmark scores while reducing inference tokens could change agent-memory architecture and evaluation choices. This remains a meaningful, bounded preprint result, not evidence of deployment-scale impact.
limitations: All performance results are author-reported in a preprint; the research desk did not independently reproduce them.
The appendix excludes adversarial settings and evaluates the Lifelong subset of WorldMemArena rather than its full suite.
The selector is trained only with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct; GPT-5-mini is used as a no-retraining transfer evaluation, leaving broader model-family and scale transfer unknown.
GPT-4o-mini supplies LLM-judge scores; no independent human-judge replication was reported in the inspected sections.
Token reduction is not a full system-cost measure: preparation/training compute, wall-clock latency, energy and production costs are not established here.
The repository is accessible and MIT-licensed, but no install, code execution or artifact reproduction occurred in this activation; dataset and model terms remain separate.
brief.summary: Zhang et al. introduce HiVe-Mem, which expands semantically retrieved interaction episodes through a text-and-visual affinity graph, then uses a PPO-trained selector to choose evidence forms per retrieved episode. In a preprint, they report higher F1 and LLM-judge scores than the compared multimodal memory systems on Mem-Gallery, WorldMemArena's Lifelong subset, and H2HMem, with 89.8–91.6% lower average token use than the most token-efficient multimodal baselines. These are author-reported benchmark results; the paper excludes adversarial settings, uses GPT-4o-mini for LLM judging, and has not been independently reproduced. The linked repository exposes implementation and experiment instructions, but the research desk did not run it.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report higher F1 and GPT-4o-mini judge scores than the compared multimodal-memory baselines on Mem-Gallery, WorldMemArena Lifelong and H2HMem, using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct and GPT-5-mini. They report mean token reductions of 91.6% and 89.8% versus the most efficient multimodal baselines for those respective models.
technical.compute_or_cost: The reported efficiency metric is combined input/output token consumption. The inspected paper does not establish total preparation/training cost, energy, wall-clock latency or deployment economics.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Nov 9 arXiv submission and its reported methodology/results are directly inspectable. The linked public GitHub repository contains source, configs, scripts and an MIT license. the research desk did not execute the repository or reproduce the benchmark measurements.
technical.implementation_status: A public GitHub repository exposes implementation, benchmark adapters, configs, scripts and experiment instructions; its README identifies the code license as MIT and notes that dataset/model licenses remain separate. The repository page showed three commits when inspected. No install, execution, or output verification occurred in this activation.
technical.mechanism: HiVe-Mem represents each text-image interaction episode with summaries, modality-aware anchors and multiple evidence forms. A sparse affinity graph expands the top semantic retrieval seeds through query-relevant shared anchors; a PPO-trained per-episode selector then chooses which summary, raw text, caption, raw image or grounded visual view to expose.
technical.novelty: Combines cross-episode affinity-based retrieval expansion with per-memory query-adaptive selection among multiple text and visual evidence forms, trained by PPO under an answer-quality/token-cost reward.
technical.regime: Three benchmark suites: Mem-Gallery, H2HMem, and the Lifelong subset of WorldMemArena; train/validation/test split 6:2:2 with adversarial settings excluded. The selector is trained using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct and transferred without retraining for GPT-5-mini evaluation. GPT-4o-mini is used as judge.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint describes methods and evaluation and links a public repository. Independent execution is unverified. The appendix excludes adversarial conditions and reports only two base models; WorldMemArena coverage is restricted to its Lifelong subset.
technical.strongest_baseline: Among the multimodal baselines in Table 1, MemVerse has the lowest average token consumption for Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (7.812M) and GPT-5-mini (7.350M); HiVe-Mem reports 0.658M and 0.748M, respectively. The table reports higher average F1 and judge scores for HiVe-Mem, but all numbers are author-reported.

brief.title: HiVe-Mem reports adaptive multimodal-memory retrieval with lower token use
brief.why_it_matters: Adaptive retrieval could help long-horizon multimodal agents retain broader episode coverage while limiting the evidence passed into each answer. If the reported tradeoff reproduces, it would change memory-system design and inference-cost evaluations. The current evidence is limited to three benchmark settings and two base models; real workloads, adversarial queries and independent results remain open.
